text:
The merit of parents

Among the signs of the merit of parents is that Allah, the Exalted, mentioned the terrors of the Day of Judgment in His saying:
يُبَصَّرُونَهُمْ ۚ يَوَدُّ الْمُجْرِمُ لَوْ يَفْتَدِي مِنْ عَذَابِ يَوْمِئِذٍ بِبَنِيهِ (11) وَصَاحِبَتِهِ وَأَخِيهِ (12) وَفَصِيلَتِهِ الَّتِي تُؤْوِيهِ (13) وَمَن فِي الْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًا ثُمَّ يُنجِيهِ

And in another place He said:
يَوْمَ يَفِرُّ الْمَرْءُ مِنْ أَخِيهِ (34) وَأُمِّهِ وَأَبِيهِ (35) وَصَاحِبَتِهِ وَبَنِيهِ

So He mentioned that a person flees from his parents, but did not mention them among those he would sacrifice, because of their standing. And Allah knows best.

قَالَ فَمَنْ رَبُّكُمَا يَا مُوسَى
He addressed the two of them (Aaron and Moses) but directed the call to just one, Moses.
This can carry two meanings:
The first is that Moses is the root of the prophethood, and Aaron is his deputy and follower.
The second is that Pharaoh used his cunning and called on Moses to do the talking, because he knew Aaron was the more eloquent of the two. It is said that Moses had a difficulty in his tongue, which is why Moses said to his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic: "وَأَخِي هَارُونُ هُوَ أَفْصَحُ مِنِّي لِسَانًا فَأَرْسِلْهُ مَعِيَ رِدْءًا يُصَدِّقُنِي"
And Pharaoh's words point to this meaning: "أَمْ أَنَا خَيْرٌ مِّنْ هَٰذَا الَّذِي هُوَ مَهِينٌ وَلَا يَكَادُ يُبِينُ" that is, I am better than this man who cannot speak clearly. And Allah knows best.

قَالَ أَرَأَيْتَ إِذْ أَوَيْنَا إِلَى الصَّخْرَةِ فَإِنِّي نَسِيتُ الْحُوتَ وَمَا أَنسَانِيهُ إِلَّا الشَّيْطَانُ أَنْ أَذْكُرَهُ ۚ وَاتَّخَذَ سَبِيلَهُ فِي الْبَحْرِ عَجَبًا
As for the word "عجبا" (amazingly), one reading is to pause after it, which makes it the words of Moses' young companion, as if he said, "How amazing was its way into the sea!" The reason for the amazement, it is said, is that the fish had been roasted and partly eaten.
The other reading is to pause before it, so that "وَاتَّخَذَ سَبِيلَهُ فِي الْبَحْرِ" is one sentence, then a stop, and then the words "عَجَبًا" as if Moses' young companion said the first sentence, and our master Moses was struck with wonder and said "How amazing!" And Allah knows best.

In my humble opinion, the most frightening verse in the Quran is: "قُلْ هَلْ نُنَبِّئُكُم بِالْأَخْسَرِينَ أَعْمَالًا (103) الَّذِينَ ضَلَّ سَعْيُهُمْ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَهُمْ يَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّهُمْ يُحْسِنُونَ صُنْعًا"
Imagine your whole life going to waste, while you were fully convinced that you were doing the right thing.

It is reported that Iblis came to Jesus (peace be upon him) and said to him: "Don't you claim that nothing will befall you except what Allah has written for you?" He said: "Yes." Iblis said: "Then throw yourself down from this mountain, for if safety is decreed for you, you will be safe." Jesus said: "Accursed one! Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, tests His servants; it is not for a servant to test his Lord."

The happiest and the most miserable thing a person can go through is to dream. The happiness is in reaching what you may never be able to reach in reality, and the misery is in knowing for certain that you will never get there.

The deed is done, you who were nothing yesterday, you whose limbs will scatter into nothing tomorrow. With what face will you meet your Lord? Is what you gain from desire worth even a word of reproach?!

Habits are another religion
I have seen that people's habits have overcome their living by the Shariah. They feel uneasy about doing a thing only because the habit isn't there, not because the Shariah forbids it!

The commentators mention that when the Prophet (peace be upon him) conquered Makkah, Uthman ibn Talha ibn Abd al-Dar hurried to lock the door of the Kaaba (he was the keeper who held its key), climbed onto its roof, and refused to hand the key to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him). He said to them: "If I knew he was the Messenger of Allah, I would not have withheld the key from him."

So Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) got up, twisted his arm, and took the key from him by force. He opened the House, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) went in, prayed two units of prayer inside the Kaaba, and came out.

Then his uncle al-Abbas asked him to give him the key, so that he would hold both the providing of water to the pilgrims and the keeping of the Kaaba. Then the words of the Almighty came down: "إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْمُرُكُمْ أَنْ تُؤَدُّوا الْأَمَانَاتِ إِلَى أَهْلِهَا وَإِذَا حَكَمْتُمْ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ أَنْ تَحْكُمُوا بِالْعَدْلِ"

So the Prophet (peace be upon him) ordered that the key be returned to Uthman ibn Talha and that an apology be made to him. When Ali went to him, Uthman said: "You hurt me and forced me, and now you come being gentle."

Ali said: "Allah has revealed a Quranic verse about you," and then recited the verse to him.

Uthman said: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad (peace be upon him) is the Messenger of Allah."

صغيرٌ يطلبُ الكِبرا .. وشيخٌ ود لو صَغُرا
وخالٍ يشتهي عملا ً.. وذو عملٍ به ضَجرا
ورب المال في تعب .. وفي تعب من افتقرا
وذو الأولاد مهمومٌ .. وطالبهم قد انفطرا
ومن فقد الجمال شكي .. وقد يشكو الذي بُهِرا
فهل حاروا مع الأقدار .. أم هم حيروا القدرا؟

A young person longs to be older, and an old man wishes he were young again.
The idle person craves work, and the one who has work is worn out by it.
The wealthy suffer in their own way, and the poor suffer too.
The one with children is full of worry, and the one who wants them is heartbroken.
The one who lacks beauty complains, and sometimes the one who is dazzled by it complains as well.
So have they been baffled by fate, or have they themselves baffled fate?
Be honorable and trustworthy, not because people deserve honor and trustworthiness, but because you do not deserve to be low and treacherous.
اللهم إني أعوذ بك من الهم و الحزن و أعوذ بك من العجز و الكسل و أعوذ بك من الجبن و البخل و أعوذ بك من غلبة الدين و قهر الرجال
Your father's anger, your mother's scolding, your friend's reproach, your brother's messing with your things, all of it is like the homeland: you don't know it is beautiful until you leave it.
أَلَمْ يَأْنِ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَن تَخْشَعَ قُلُوبُهُمْ لِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ؟

إلهي لا تعذبني فإني
مقرٌّ بالذي قد كان مني

وما لي حيلةٌ إلا رجائي
وعفوك إن عفوتَ وحسن ظني

My God, do not punish me, for I admit to all that I have done.

I have no resort but my hope, and Your pardon if You pardon, and my good opinion of You.

The Prophet (peace be upon him) said to Hakim ibn Hizam: "يا حكيم، إن هذا المال خَضِرةٌ حلوة، فمن أخذه بسخاوة نفسٍ بورك له فيه، ومن أخذه بإشراف نفسٍ لم يبارك له فيه، كالذي يأكل ولا يشبع"

Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar (may Allah have mercy on him) said:
In it is a parable for something the listener cannot grasp by reason alone, because most people only recognize blessing (barakah) in abundance. So through this parable he showed that blessing is a creation of Allah, the Exalted, and he gave them an example from what they know: a person eats in order to be satisfied, so if he eats and is not satisfied, it is only hardship for him with no benefit. Likewise wealth: its benefit is not in itself but in the advantages gained through it, so if a person has much of it without drawing any benefit from it, its existence is like its absence.

O you! Worship Allah for what He wants from you, not for what you want from Him. Whoever worships Him for what he wants from Him is among those who worship Allah on the edge: if good befalls him, he is content with it, and if a trial befalls him, he turns back on his face, losing this world and the Hereafter. And when knowledge and love grow strong, the one who has them wants nothing except what his Master wants.
Whoever has a regular daily portion of worship and abandons it, I fear for him that the sweetness of worship will be taken from him.

It used to be said: six people who are humiliated should blame no one but themselves: the one who goes to a table he was not invited to; the one who seeks generosity from the ignoble; the one who enters into the conversation of two people without being let in; the one who belittles the ruler; the one who sits in a seat he is not worthy of; and the one who turns with his talk to someone who neither listens to him nor pays him any attention.

A man came to Imam al-Ishbili to ask him a question: "What is a kamawj?"
Al-Ishbili said: "Where did you read it?"
The man replied: "In the verse of Imru' al-Qays: 'Wa laylin ka-mawji l-bahri arkha sudulah' (a night like the waves of the sea, which let down its curtains)."
Al-Ishbili said: "Kamawj is an animal that reads but does not understand!"
(The man had split the words wrongly: it is "ka-mawj", meaning "like the waves", not one word.)

The Messenger of Allah’s (peace be upon him) pleasure was dearer to me than the world and all that is in it!

Once the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) was traveling from Ta’if to al-Ji’ranah, with Abu Ruhm al-Ghifari beside him on his camel, wearing a pair of thick sandals.

His camel crowded the camel of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him). Abu Ruhm said: "The edge of my sandal landed on his leg and hurt him. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: «أوجعتني أخر رجلك», and he tapped my foot with his whip."

He said: "All my past and future worries seized me, and I feared that a Qur’anic verse would be revealed about me because of the gravity of what I had done."

"When morning came at al-Ji’ranah, I went out to graze the camels, though it was not my turn, out of fear that a messenger would come for me. When I brought the animals back, I asked, and they said: ‘The Prophet (peace be upon him) asked for you.’ I said: ‘By Allah, it has happened.’"

"I came to him, trembling, and he said: «إنك أوجعتني برجلك فقرعتك بالسوط وأوجعتك فخذ هذه الغنم عوضا من ضربتي»"

Abu Ruhm said: "His being pleased with me was dearer to me than the world and all that is in it."

O Allah, we ask You for Your pleasure and the pleasure of Your Messenger!
You will never find a seeker of anything who will not, one day, have his fill of it, except the seeker of knowledge and the seeker of this world.

Abd al-Rahman ibn Harmalah asked Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab: "I found a man drunk. Do you think I may refrain from reporting him to the authorities?"
Sa’id said to him: "If you can cover him with your garment, then cover him."

The Prophet (peace be upon him) also said to Hazzal al-Aslami, after Hazzal had told Ma’iz ibn Malik to confess adultery to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him). Ma’iz was married, so the punishment was carried out on him, and he had been an orphan in Hazzal’s care: «يا هزّال بئس ما صنعت بيتيمك! لو سترت عليه بطرف ردائك لكان خيرًا لك!»

Whenever a man sat with Ibn Abi Dhi’b and became a regular in his circle, Ibn Abi Dhi’b would ask the people there: "What has become of your companion?"

If they said, "We do not know,"
he would ask: "Where is his house?"
If they said, "We do not know,"
he would be annoyed with them and say: "What are you good for? A man sits with you and you do not know about him! If he falls ill, you do not visit him, and if he has a need, you do not help him!" And if they knew his house, he would say: "Get up, let us go to him at his home, ask after him and visit him."

As for getting into the habit of speaking in a language other than Arabic, which is the emblem of Islam and the language of the Qur’an, until this becomes the custom of a city and its people, or of the people of a household, or of a man with his friend, or of the people of the marketplace, or of the rulers, or of the officials, or of the jurists: there is no doubt that this is disliked, for it is imitation of the non-Arabs, and that is disliked, as has preceded.

For this reason, when the early Muslims settled in the lands of Syria and Egypt, whose people spoke Greek, and in Iraq and Khurasan, whose people spoke Persian, and in the Maghreb, whose people spoke Berber, they accustomed the people of those lands to Arabic, until it prevailed over the inhabitants of these cities, Muslim and non-Muslim alike. Khurasan was likewise in the past. And know that the habit of a language strongly and clearly affects the mind, the character and the religion, and it also affects resemblance to the first generations of this nation, the Companions and the Successors, and resembling them increases one’s intellect, religion and character.

Moreover, the Arabic language itself is part of the religion, and knowing it is an obligatory duty, because understanding the Book and the Sunnah is an obligation, and they cannot be understood without understanding Arabic, and whatever an obligation cannot be fulfilled without is itself obligatory.

The manners of the grammarians

In parsing "الرحمن الرحيم" in the Basmala, al-Kafrawi mentions six possible readings, among them the accusative of veneration, with an omitted verb understood: (أقصدُ) الرحمنَ الرحيمَ, "I mean the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful". After listing these readings he says:
You now know that the accusative among them is accusative for veneration through an omitted verb, and that the nominative is a predicate of an omitted subject. And the accusative is not called "direct object", out of courtesy toward Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Know that night and day are twenty-four hours, so let your sleep, by night and day together, be no more than eight hours. If you live, say, sixty years, it is enough that you lose twenty of them, which is a third of your life.

The world is a trap. The ignorant falls at the first glance. As for the wise and God-fearing, he endures hunger and circles around the grain, and safety is far off. How many a patient one strove for years, only to fall in the end! So beware, beware. We have seen someone on the path of what is right who then slipped at the very edge of the grave.

It is reported that al-Hallaj the Sufi used to sit in the sun in the fiercest heat, his sweat running down. One of the wise passed by and said to him: "Fool, this is showing off your strength against Allah, the Exalted!"
How well he put it! For obligations were only set against our desires, and a person may be pushed until he can no longer endure. The ignorant fool is the one who acts mighty before Allah, or who asks for hardship, like that simpleton who said: "Test me however You wish" (that is, "O Lord, test me as You will", not knowing that he may not be able to bear the affliction).
